episode_row: deploy pull failed on uv.lock drift; stale code while CI green

commits.subject: fix(deploy): prevent silent deploy failures from uv.lock drift
commits.body:
Root cause: Mac has ~/.config/uv/uv.toml with exclude-newer = "3 days"
(supply-chain defense per Willison's "package managers need to cool down"
post). bts-mlb had no matching global config, so its uv dropped the
[options] section from uv.lock on every `uv run`. Every commit touching
uv.lock would silently fail the `git pull --ff-only` step, and the
workflow script had no `set -e`, so services would restart on stale code
with the GitHub Actions run still showing green. This session's
catboost commit was the first uv.lock change in 3 days and tripped it.

Three fixes together:

1. Move exclude-newer into pyproject.toml [tool.uv] with an absolute
   date ("2026-04-11") instead of the relative "3 days" value. Project
   config overrides user config, so both Mac and bts-mlb now produce
   byte-identical uv.lock files. Update this line manually when
   refreshing the supply-chain window.

2. Add `set -e` to the deploy workflow script so any failing step
   (git pull, uv sync, systemctl) halts the deploy and turns the GH
   Actions run red. No more silent green-on-broken.

3. Add `uv sync --locked --extra model` as a post-pull validation step.
   Errors out if uv.lock drifts from pyproject.toml, and installs any
   newly-declared deps into the venv (fixes the chronic "production
   missing an optional dep" class of problem).

Also: run git pull and uv sync as `sudo -Hu bts` rather than root, so
pulled files keep bts ownership and uv reads bts's home config.
